mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 4% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE exceeds 4% but S&P 500 returns remain positive more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When federal funds rate is above 5% and unemployment is below 4%, it may indicate tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the condition is met but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, higher federal funds rates predict negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS increases but S&P 500 returns remain positive more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production suggests strong supply, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI increase above 5% indicates inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL exceeds 5% but S&P 500 returns remain positive more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When payroll employment increases and real federal funds rate decreases, it signals economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: If the condition is met but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, increasing housing starts predict positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.
